channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Breaking: ADP Employment Change declines to 44K in July vs. 70K expected
item.description: Employment in the United States' (US) private sector increased by 44K in July, the Automatic Data Processing (ADP) reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Copper: Tight supply supports breakout above $14,000 – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Copper has surged above $14,000 per tonne on the LME, driven by tightening physical conditions and strong prompt demand.

item.title: US Dollar: Consolidation view into ISM and payrolls – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the Dollar is mixed as global equities rise and Oil stabilizes. Haddad argues the USD rally from May has likely ended, with US Dollar Index (DXY) expected to consolidate in a 96.00–100.00 range.

item.title: Brent: Price slips on Hormuz deal hopes – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Daily notes Brent futures fell to around $79 as reports suggested the US, Iran and Oman are close to a temporary deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Trades near crucial level of 1.1550
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades 0.15% higher at around 1.1550 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The major currency pair gains as the US Dollar faces selling pressure ahead of a busy North American session.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD, capped below $62.00 but steady near one-month highs
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) has found some resistance at the $61.90 area on Wednesday, before pulling back to $61.24 at the moment of writing, but remains above the top of the last four weeks’ range, at the $60.90 area.

item.title: Euro: PMI resilience tempers stagflation fears – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes Eurozone PMIs have surprised to the upside, with the composite at an eight‑month high and services back in expansion, easing immediate stagflation worries.

item.title: Gold advances to one-month high as Hormuz reopening hopes ease inflation fears
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) climbs to a one-month high on Wednesday as renewed optimism over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz sends Oil prices lower. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,155, up nearly 1.90% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Soft labor firmer services outlook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists notes that United States (US) JOLTS job openings fell more than expected in June, though they remain elevated versus private indicators. They also expect the United States (US) ISM Services Index to rise in July, projecting 55.0 versus June’s 54.0 and a consensus of 54.5.

item.title: United States Dollar Index trades subduedly below 100.00 ahead of US data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) reflects a subdued performance against its peers ahead of the United States (US) ADP Employment Change and the ISM Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data for July, which will be published in the North American session.

item.title: WTI recovers part of its losses, caught between technical rebound, diplomatic optimism
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades around $75.50 on Wednesday at the time of writing, up 1.56% on the day, as investors take advantage of a technical rebound following the more than 5% decline recorded in the previous day.

item.title: British Pound extends gains to 212.50 against the Yen after upbeat UK services data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends gains for the second consecutive day against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Wednesday, with the GBP/JPY pair holding around 212.30 after bouncing from five-month lows at 209.55 on Monday.

item.title: Indian Rupee surrenders some gains, RBI maintain status quo again
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) surrenders some gains after a strong opening against the US Dollar (USD), following the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Dovish MPC hold supports prolonged pause – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered Bank economists Saurav Anand and Anubhuti Sahay note that India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) kept the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance, sounding more dovish than in April and June.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Gains seen while below 160.00 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann describe USD/JPY price action as muted, with the pair confined to 157.15–157.95 and momentum turning flat. They expect intraday range trading between 157.00 and 158.30.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hits fresh weekly highs beyond the top of a triangle pattern
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) has accelerated its recovery on Wednesday, favoured by a softer US Dollar as lower Oil prices and downbeat US macroeconomic data cooled market expectations of Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes on Tuesday.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: MPC minutes key for support against Euro – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose explains that the Hungarian Forint (HUF) has recently given back gains as external shocks and an ongoing Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) easing cycle erode support.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $61.52 per troy ounce, up 2.87% from the $59.81 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar comes under pressure after sharp deterioration in labor market
item.description: NZD/USD declines to around 0.5860 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.54% on the day, following the release of weaker-than-expected New Zealand employment data. The New Zealand Dollar (USD) comes under selling pressure as investors reassess the outlook for monetary policy.

item.title: Danish Krone: Weakness seen as structural against Euro – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Chief Analyst Jan Størup Nielsen notes that Nationalbanken did not intervene in July to support Denmark’s fixed exchange rate policy, after a small purchase of kroner in June.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Trades around 1.3450; bulls retain control above 100-hour SMA
item.description: The GBP/USD pair gains follow-through positive traction for the second straight day and sticks to modest intraday gains through the first half of the European session on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro gains against Canadian Dollar following improved PMI data
item.description: EUR/CAD continues its winning streak that started on July 24, trading around 1.6240 during the European hours on Wednesday. The currency cross rises as the Euro (EUR) receives support following the release of HCOB Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) data from Germany and the Eurozone.

item.title: ISM Services PMI Preview: US services sector expected to accelerate in July
item.description: On Wednesday, we’ll get the latest read on the US services sector when the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) publishes its July gauge. Consensus points to a marginal improvement to 54.5 from June’s 54.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Negative bias builds with policy headwinds – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research strategist Philip Wee notes that the US Dollar Index (DXY) Index is struggling to regain the 100 level, with European currencies better reflecting underlying Dollar weakness once Japanese Yen (JPY) volatility is excluded.

item.title: Japan's Katayama sees inflation easing with tax reduction
item.description: Japan Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama said during the European trading session on Wednesday that the government's tax policy would be able to cool down high inflation.

item.title: Australian Dollar flattens against USD in countdown to US ADP labor data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades flat against the US Dollar (USD) at around 0.7050 during the European trading session on Wednesday. The Aussie pair struggles for a direction as investors await the United States (US) ADP Employment Change data for July, which will be published at 12:15 GMT.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy follow-up needed for renewed demand – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that coordinated intervention has not significantly increased foreign exposure to the Japanese Yen (JPY), with investors still net long JPY but at much lower levels than in H1 2026.

item.title: Dow Jones futures gain on expected US-Iran agreement to reopen Hormuz
item.description: Dow Jones futures rise 0.23% to trade around 54,390 during European hours on Wednesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures gain 0.34% to trade near 7,790, while Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.14%, trading near 29,900.

item.title: Euro steadies around 1.1540 after an upward revision of Eurozone's Services PMI
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the EUR/USD pair consolidating around the 1.1530 area, a few pips below seven-week highs at 1.1558.

item.title: Gold clings to gains near one-month top as receding Fed rate hike bets undermine USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its strong bid tone through the first half of the European session and currently trades around $4,170, just below a nearly one-month high touched earlier this Wednesday.
